scope: Canonical map of the Marvell/ASR CI (Common Interface) primitive layer that carries AP-to-CP modem control on M7000(EU) v3.2 firmware 3.0.2 Build 241129 Rel.3n. Recovered statically from bin/atcmdsrv name tables and from the CP image 05-ARBI.bin at its confirmed load base. No primitive was constructed, sent, or observed on a live device.
why_this_layer_matters: AT text does not cross the AP/CP boundary. atcmdsrv parses the AT command and emits a binary CI primitive over the shared-memory transport, so the CI primitive set - not the AT vocabulary - is the real control surface between the two processors.

source.table_form: arrays of pointers to NUL-terminated primitive-name strings, one array per CI service group

service_groups.table_va: 0x0b2fa4 (atcmdsrv, biased base; slot 0 is a shared empty-string placeholder, so the table is indexed directly by the numeric service-group id)
service_groups.numbering: CONFIRMED 1-based. A previous revision of this file recorded these ids as 0-based (CC=0 ... OAM=13); that was an artefact of counting the placeholder slot as entry 0 and is superseded.
decisive_evidence: atcmdsrv 0x7de58: `ldr.w r3,[r0, r5, lsl #2]` indexes the group-name table with r5 = the raw svgId argument, not svgId-1.
atcmdsrv 0x7ddf0: `add.w r8, r0, #-1` then `cmp r3,#0xd` bounds svgId-1 to 0..13, i.e. svgId 1..14.
ARBI 0x068afe7a and 0x068b010a both load `movs r0, #9` as the service group when emitting a DEV error / confirmation, matching DEV = 9.

primitive_id_encoding.rule: The numeric wire primitive id is the 1-based index into that service group's own name table. There is no group field packed into the id: (service_group, primId) is carried as two separate wire fields.

global_error_range.meaning: A single global primitive range shared by all service groups, indexed as primId - 0xF000 into a separate table at atcmdsrv 0x0b2440.
global_error_range.correction: A previous revision recorded CI_ERR as occupying DEV indices 246-254. That was wrong: the CI_ERR name strings merely sit next to the DEV table in memory. The dispatcher at atcmdsrv 0x7de1e tests `primId <= 0xF007` and 0x7deac tests `(primId + 0x1000) & 0xFFFF <= 7` before any group dispatch, proving CI_ERR is a separate namespace reached without consulting the service group.

decisive_evidence: Every group name table's slot 0 holds the same pointer (atcmdsrv 0x000979f0, an empty string), i.e. a placeholder for the unused id 0.
The dispatcher at atcmdsrv 0x7ddec loads each group table from a base biased by -4 and indexes it with the raw primId (`ldr.w r3,[r1, r4, lsl #2]`), which is only correct for 1-based ids.
atcmdsrv 0x40cac (the AT*BAND request builder) emits `movs r1, #0x33` = 51 = the table index of CI_DEV_PRIM_SET_BAND_MODE_REQ.
ARBI 0x068b0108 emits `movs r1, #0x34` = 52 = CI_DEV_PRIM_SET_BAND_MODE_CNF as the reply.
ARBI 0x068afe7c emits `movw r1, #0xf001` = CI_ERR_PRIM_HASINVALIDPARAS_CNF on parameter failure.
The CP DEV request-dispatch table at ARBI 0x6f394fc pairs primId 0x33 with handler 0x068afdf1, and all 76 of its ids resolve to *_REQ names under this numbering.
primitive_id_encoding.validated_across: Five primitives (0x33, 0x34, 0x35, 0x37, 0xF001) from two independent binaries on opposite sides of the AP/CP boundary, plus a 76-entry CP dispatch table whose every entry resolves to a _REQ name.

refuted_hypothesis.hypothesis: primId = (service_group_id << 8) | index, which would make the compiler hold a biased table pointer of (table - 4*(sg<<8)).
refuted_hypothesis.test: For CI_DEV (group 8) that biased pointer would be 0x0b2068 - 0x2000 = 0x0b0068, and a word equal to 0x000b0068 does occur in atcmdsrv at VA 0x7ad10.
refuted_hypothesis.result: REFUTED. 0x0b0068 is the address of the ASCII string 'mrvl_gps_integrity_test', and the referencing function is an unrelated AT handler. Only 1 of 9 groups produced any match at shift 8, and shifts 9, 10, 12 and 16 produced 0 or 1 coincidental matches. The apparent hit is a collision, not an encoding.

DAT.payload_size_rule: DAT payload sizes are computed at run time by atcmdsrv 0x7ef30 from the payload itself, not read from a table.

DEV.note: This table holds the CI_DEV group at indices 0-245 (index 245 is CI_DEV_PRIM_LAST_COMMON_PRIM) followed by the CI_ERR group at indices 246-254. CI_ERR has no separate table.

request_dispatch_table_cp.form: 76 entries of {u32 primId, u32 handler|1} (8-byte stride)
request_dispatch_table_cp.verification: Every id resolves to a CI_DEV_PRIM_*_REQ name under the confirmed numbering; primId 0x33 pairs with 0x068afdf1, the independently proven SET_BAND_MODE handler.

anchor.name: CI_DEV_PRIM_SET_BAND_MODE_REQ
anchor.index_in_group: 51 (1-based; a previous revision said 50 by counting the placeholder slot)
anchor.ap_origin: AT*BAND, parsed by the atcmdsrv AT dispatch entry at VA 0xdb8ac whose handler is the Thumb function at VA 0x3813c

cp_handler.identification: Reached from the AT*BAND log string at VA 0x068b03cc, which is referenced by an ADR at VA 0x068b0134, and from the two assertion strings referenced at VA 0x068b009c and 0x068b0082.

request_struct.validation: passed to helper at VA 0x068afdb4; bit 9 tested via lsls #22

request_struct.field: band mask C/D (LTE band pair, loaded with ldrd)

cp_handler.range_check_failure: Out-of-range fields return through the error path at VA 0x068afe7a with code 0xf001.
cp_handler.confidence: CONFIRMED for offsets, widths and the range checks; UNKNOWN for the names of the fields at 0x14, 0x15, 0x16 and 0x1c.

cp_enum_finding.observed_logic: When networkMode is 0, 1 or 3 the handler requires preferredMode == networkMode (assertion 'pSig->preferredMode == pSig->networkMode', line 3767). When networkMode is 2 or >= 4 it requires preferredMode to be one of 0, 1 or 3 (assertion 'pSig->preferredMode == CI_DEV_NW_GSM || pSig->preferredMode == CI_DEV_NW_UMTS || pSig->preferredMode == CI_DEV_NW_LTE', line 3760).
cp_enum_finding.direct_consequence: CI_DEV_NW_GSM, CI_DEV_NW_UMTS and CI_DEV_NW_LTE are exactly the set {0, 1, 3}. Values 2, 4, 5 and 6 are multi-RAT combinations, because they are the values for which a separate single-RAT preference is required.

individual_assignment.basis: the order of the equality tests (0, 1, 3) matches the order of the symbols in the assertion text

subset_interpretation.claim: networkMode enumerates the 7 non-empty subsets of {GSM, UMTS, LTE} as (bitmask - 1) with GSM=1, UMTS=2, LTE=4, giving GSM=0, UMTS=1, GSM+UMTS=2, LTE=3, GSM+LTE=4, UMTS+LTE=5, all=6.
subset_interpretation.basis: It is the unique assignment that puts the singletons at exactly {0, 1, 3}, matches the observed range check of < 7, and matches the singleton/combination split the handler enforces.
subset_interpretation.classification: SUPPORTED INFERENCE - self-consistent and strongly constrained, but the enum definition itself was not recovered.

cp_enum_finding.important_distinction: This CI networkMode space (0-6) is NOT the AT*BAND textual NwMode space. The AP sends AT*BAND=0/1/5/11 with default 99 and recognises 0/4/5/8/11/15 on readback, all of which exceed or contradict a 0-6 enum. atcmdsrv therefore translates between them, and that translation is not yet recovered.

anchor.mutation_status: NOT EXECUTED. No CI primitive was built or sent.
payload_size_evidence: The DEV size table at 0x0bda4e holds 32 at index 51.
anchor.namespace_collision_warning: CI_DEV_PRIM_SET_BAND_MODE_REQ is primId 0x33 and the AP libmobile/mobile preferred-RAT event is also id 0x33. These are unrelated numbers in unrelated namespaces (CI primitive id vs CMobileEvent id) that happen to coincide. Do not treat one as evidence for the other.

numeric_spaces_now_known: UI / configured policy enum (AP record 75 `mobile_config.net_config.pref_net`), values 0-3.
AT*BAND textual NwMode, accepted range 0..30 with default 240; only 0..15 and 240 are handled.
CI networkMode / preferredMode, 0..6, the RAT bitmask minus one (GSM=1, UMTS=2, LTE=4).
CP internal RAT state, 0..6, singletons first then pairs; translated to CI space by the tbb tables at ARBI 0x068b0192 and 0x068b01c2.
AP modem readback enum used by mobile 0x4a254, values 0-3.
CI numeric primitive id, per service group, 1-based, plus the global 0xF000 error range.
safety: Static recovery only. The presence of a primitive name, index, or request structure is not evidence that it is reachable, permitted, or safe to invoke.

ap_sender_catalogue.method: Every BL/B.W to the CI send stub at atcmdsrv 0x7cd14 was enumerated (397 sites); for each, the primitive id was taken from the immediate that sets r1 and the service group from the CI client-object slot, using the confirmed rule slot_offset = 4 * svgId.
ap_sender_catalogue.validation: 392 of 397 sites resolve to a name ending in _REQ under this model. The residue is 5 sites: one where the primitive id is loaded from a register rather than an immediate, and CI_SIM_PRIM_RSAP_STATUS_IND (an indication genuinely sent AP-to-CP).
ap_sender_catalogue.why_it_matters: This replaces one-by-one recovery from isolated handlers. Any CI primitive reachable from an AT command can now be looked up rather than reverse-engineered.

client_object_table.rule: The CI client-object table is indexed by service group id; the slot offset is 4 * svgId.
client_object_table.evidence: Applied blind to all 397 send sites it yields a valid _REQ name 392 times; the DEV slot +0x24 independently matches the already-proven SET_BAND_MODE path.
client_object_table.corroborates: The 1-based service-group numbering, since a 0-based numbering would shift every slot.
